candidate.answerReason: The last digit is 3 exactly when b≥4 and b divides 2010. The number 2010 has 16 positive divisors, of which 1, 2, and 3 are invalid bases for that digit.

methods.label: Translate the last digit into a divisor condition
methods.explanation:
In base \(b\), every place except the units place contributes a multiple of \(b\). Thus ending in the digit \(3\) means that dividing \(2013\) by \(b\) leaves remainder \(3\). The digit must also be smaller than the base, so \(b\ge4\).

We therefore need
\[
2013=bq+3,
\qquad bq=2010
\]
for a positive integer \(q\). Conversely, every divisor \(b\ge4\) of \(2010\) gives this equation with \(3<b\), so it really does give last digit \(3\).

Factor
\[
2010=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot67.
\]
These are four distinct primes. A positive divisor includes or excludes each prime independently, giving \(2^4=16\) divisors. Unique prime factorization ensures that these choices include every divisor exactly once.

The divisors \(1\), \(2\), and \(3\) do not satisfy \(b\ge4\); all the others do. Hence the number of valid bases is
\[
16-3=\boxed{13},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
